phase_0.boundary_condition: verified prime pair whose product equals input N sealed in classical memory

AFWD.chosen_element: modular exponentiation followed by quantum Fourier transform
AFWD.justification: drives exponent superposition forward toward phase peaks that encode the period

AREV.chosen_element: return from failed continued fraction to fresh base selection
AREV.justification: steps back down from rejection toward a new preparation cycle

CLINK.chosen_element: Hadamard preparation chained into modular exponentiation chained into Fourier transform
CLINK.justification: links three unitary stages into one ordered pipeline acting on control and work registers

ENGAGR.chosen_element: coexisting rival convergents from noisy phase readout
ENGAGR.justification: holds competing period candidates live together before greatest common divisor testing selects among them

EVALF.chosen_element: odd period or trivial root with no factor yield
EVALF.justification: negative condition that refutes the shot and calls for another base or exponent range

EVALT.chosen_element: even period r with a to power r over 2 not congruent to minus one mod N
EVALT.justification: affirmative condition that lets greatest common divisor expose nontrivial factors

FFUSE.chosen_element: hypothesis arms rejoining into one factor set
FFUSE.justification: merges validated factors and retried shots into a single resolved factor set

FSPLIT.chosen_element: phase estimate opening into period hypotheses
FSPLIT.justification: opens one phase estimate into an affirming arm and a rejecting arm

IFIX.chosen_element: collapsed bitstring and verified factor pair written to classical storage
IFIX.justification: creates an append only record that cannot be unmeasured or unfactored

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: periodic function recognizing its own shift f(x+r) equal to f(x)
IMSCRIB.justification: expresses self sameness of the modular exponential across one period interval

TANCH.chosen_element: sealed classical record holding p and q with p times q equal to N
TANCH.justification: contains the complete factorization and stops further quantum shots

VINIT.chosen_element: composite integer N with no assigned factors
VINIT.justification: marks the empty factoring task before registers are prepared and base a is chosen
